name: Deaf Transcribe:Speech to Text
oneLine: An iPhone app that turns speech around you into live text in 71 languages, free to download with a paid Pro subscription; sold on the App Store by Youdao Education Technology (Hong Kong).

platforms.detail: Apple's App Store lists it as "Only for iPhone"; it also runs on Apple Vision. A Google Play search on 28 October 2026 found no Android version, and the developer website links only to the App Store.

deviceRequirements.detail: The App Store lists iOS 13.0 or later for iPhone, and visionOS 1.0 or later for Apple Vision.

roomCaptions.text: Yes, speech around you as live text
roomCaptions.detail: The listing says it instantly turns speech into text so people who are hard of hearing can follow conversations. The developer website says "Hear what others are saying, anywhere, anytime."

groupConversations.detail: The listing and website don't describe group conversations, external microphones or joining several phones into one conversation.

languages.detail: The listing says you can transcribe, record and create captions in 71 languages and names each one, from English, Spanish, Chinese and Arabic to Cantonese, Swahili and Zulu. The app's own menus come in 7 languages.

offline.detail: The listing doesn't mention working without internet. The terms describe the service as provided via the internet and make you responsible for connecting.

speakerLabels.detail: Neither the listing nor the website describes showing who is talking. One App Store screenshot shows lines under the name "Dr. James", but no text explains it.

translation.detail: The listing names 71 caption languages but doesn't describe translating speech into another language.

saveTranscripts.text: Yes, text saved in the app
saveTranscripts.detail: The listing says you can save the converted text in the app, and that the app can record. The terms list unlimited recordings as a Pro feature; the free version's limit isn't stated.

export.text: Share via email, messaging and social apps
export.detail: Saved text can be shared by email, messaging apps or social media; a store screenshot shows Copy and Copy Photo options. File formats aren't stated.

fileUpload.detail: The listing describes live speech-to-text, not transcribing audio or video files you already have.

summaries.detail: No AI summaries or notes are described in the listing or on the website.

customWords.detail: The listing doesn't describe adding your own words or names.

display.text: Font sizes, colours, themes; flip and type
display.detail: The listing says you can choose font sizes, colors and themes. Store screenshots show buttons to type, flip the text for the person opposite, adjust the text (Aa) and clear the screen.

soundAlerts.detail: The listing describes speech-to-text only; no alerts for sounds such as a doorbell or an alarm are described.

phoneCalls.detail: The listing doesn't describe captioning phone calls.

videoCalls.detail: The listing doesn't describe captioning Zoom, Teams or FaceTime calls.

mediaOnDevice.detail: The listing doesn't describe captioning videos or audio playing on the phone.

humanCaptioners.detail: The listing describes automatic speech recognition; no human captioner option is described.

signLanguage.detail: No sign language features are described in the listing or on the website.

privacy.text: Not stated where; policy covers audio, US servers
privacy.detail: The listing doesn't say whether speech is turned into text on the phone or on a server; the terms say the service runs via the internet. The privacy policy (September 2023) lets the company collect audio recordings and the text of words spoken, says data may be stored on servers in the United States, names Alibaba Cloud, Firebase, Google, Facebook, Apple and App Annie as service providers, and allows sharing some data with Facebook to build ad audiences; it says personal information is not sold. Apple's privacy label lists identifiers that may be used to track you. Whether audio is used to train AI is not stated.

account.text: Not clear; some versions need no login
account.detail: The listing says you can delete your data from your account. The terms say you may log in with a phone number or a third-party account, and that some versions have no login, with Pro linked to your Apple ID.

availability.text: App Store in many countries; not Hong Kong
availability.detail: Apple's store data finds it in the US and UK App Stores (and other countries checked), but not in the Hong Kong store, on 28 October 2026. No country list is published.

freePlan.text: Free download; Pro removes ads, unlimited recordings
freePlan.detail: The app is free to download, with in-app purchases. The terms say Pro adds ad removal and unlimited recordings; the free version's limits aren't stated. The listing describes a 3-day free trial for its subscription.

price.text: Pro: US$5.99 or US$49.99 (periods not listed)
price.detail: Apple's US App Store lists two "Live Transcribe Pro" purchases, US$5.99 and US$49.99 (October 2026), without saying which period each covers. The description names a 1-week subscription with a 3-day free trial; the terms mention weekly, monthly and annual subscriptions.

accessibilityFunding.detail: No funding through a government or insurance programme is described.

strengths.text: Captions speech in 71 languages, each one named on the App Store listing.
Runs on iPhones with iOS 13 or later, and on Apple Vision.
Font sizes, colours and themes can be changed, and store screenshots show buttons to type a reply and flip the text for the person opposite.
Free to download, and the listing describes a 3-day free trial of Pro.

limits.text: iPhone only: no Android version was found on Google Play.
The listing describes no speaker labels, translation, file transcription or AI summaries.
Apple's listing doesn't say which subscription period each Pro price covers.
The last App Store update was version 1.3.0 on 5 September 2025, and the privacy policy is dated September 2023.

quotes: Only for iPhone
It instantly turns speech into text, making it easy for people who are hard of hearing to follow conversations.
You can transcribe, record, and create captions in 71 languages.
It even works with deaf voice dictation, turning spoken words into text quickly and accurately.
With cutting-edge speech recognition technology, our app guarantees a high level of accuracy in converting audio to text, making it incredibly reliable for all users.
Choose from different font sizes, colors, and themes to enhance your reading experience.
Save the converted text files directly within the app and easily share them via email, messaging apps, or social media platforms.

notes: Names: the App Store seller is YOUDAO EDUCATION TECHNOLOGY (HONG KONG) LIMITED (developer id 1813052831; its other app is Smart AI Note Taker: MemoWave). Youdao, Inc.'s 2024 Form 20-F (SEC) lists Youdao Education Technology (Hong Kong) Limited as a 100% subsidiary and calls NetEase, Inc. its controlling shareholder. The privacy policy (updated 5 September 2023) and terms name TALENT ME TECHNOLOGY PTE. LTD. (Singapore) as the company that runs the service, the listing's copyright reads '© 2023 Talent Me Limited', and Youdao's 20-F does not mention Talent Me, so how the two are linked is not stated. The terms are governed by Chinese law with CIETAC arbitration in Beijing. The app calls itself 'Live Transcribe' in its privacy policy, terms, website title and in-app purchase name ('Live Transcribe Pro'); it is not Google's Live Transcribe. Other apps with similar names on the App Store are by different developers: 'Deaf Transcriber : HearingPal' (Burotec Limited), 'Deaf Transcribe Assistant', 'Speech to Text for Deaf', and 'Live Transcribe' (Mighty Fine Apps LLC); on Google Play, 'UHO Global - deaf transcribe' is also unrelated. Conflict: the App Store description says data 'will not be transferred to third parties for any reason', while the privacy policy lists third-party service providers (Alibaba Cloud, Firebase, Google, Facebook, Apple, App Annie), sharing of identifiers and usage with analytics and measurement partners, and sharing with Facebook for Custom or Lookalike Audiences; Apple's privacy label lists identifiers used to track you. Prices: the US In-App Purchases list shows 'Live Transcribe Pro' at $5.99 and $49.99 with no period; the description names only a 1-week subscription with a 3-day free trial; the terms mention weekly/monthly/annual subscriptions and give no prices. Periods were not assumed. Free-version limits: the terms say Pro removes ads and gives unlimited recordings; no free limit is stated, and whether the free version shows ads is only implied. Where speech is processed (on the phone or on a server) is not stated anywhere; the terms only say the service is provided via the internet. The developer website (livetranscribe.luckon.online) renders with JavaScript; its text was read from the page's own script bundle. That bundle has a footer component naming NetEase Youdao Information Technology (Beijing) Co., Ltd. with a Beijing address, but it is switched off (not shown), so it is not used as a source. One store screenshot shows caption lines under the name 'Dr. James'; no text describes speaker labels, so speakerLabels is not_stated. Availability: Apple's lookup found the app in the US, UK, Canada, Australia, Germany, France, Spain, Italy, Brazil, Mexico, India, South Korea, mainland China, Japan, Taiwan and Singapore stores, and not in Hong Kong (28 October 2026). Google Play: no Android version found by search; the Google Play developer page of Youdao (Hong Kong) Limited lists six other apps and no captions app. Ratings, reviews and download counts on the listing were not used. Not checked: in-app behaviour, the free version's ads or limits, and accuracy.
